data.name: Haifa
data.gender_notes: Haifa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Haifa means gardens. It is a name of spiritual significance in Islam, as it is believed to derive from the story of the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Quran. The name evokes images of paradise and growth, symbolizing the nurturing and cultivation of faith and good deeds. The name Haifa carries the meaning “Gardens” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haifa usually hope their child will grow to embody gardens and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and growth.
data.etymology: Haifa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardens.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haifa total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.meaning: اسم علم مؤنث يعني الجمال والخير

in_urdu.name: حیفہ

in_english.name: Haifa
in_english.long_meaning: Haifa is an Arabic name that means beauty and goodness, derived from the city of Haifa in Palestine, and holds special significance in Islamic culture and tradition

data.cultural_impact: Haifa is a city in Israel and Palestine, known for its rich history and multicultural population. The name Haifa holds cultural significance due to its association with the city, which has long been a center of trade and cultural exchange. In more recent times, it has been known for its beautiful gardens, which attract tourists from around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: Haifa is also a name of spiritual significance in Islam. It is believed that the name derives from the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Quran, in which he interprets dreams for his father, Jacob, and promises him that he will be with him in a "lush paradise, with rivers flowing underneath" (Quran 12:100). This promise is understood by some scholars to refer to the city of Haifa, which is known for its beautiful gardens and lush landscape. The name Haifa therefore evokes images of paradise and growth, symbolizing the nurturing and cultivation of faith and good deeds.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Prophet Muhammad's companion, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, was known to have a daughter named Haifa. The name Haifa carried significant weight in that era.
